head: 704741b8aa2dbcde2e9560cce086f831c4b767c7
headline: The admin users page gains delete and change-role buttons, but anyone online can use them, signed in or not.
what_changed: Each row on the admin users page now has a drop-down to set the person's role to member, manager or admin.
Each row also has a Delete button. It asks for confirmation, then permanently removes the user and all their shifts.
Two new web addresses the app answers were added to carry out the role change and the delete.
The patch was applied exactly as provided, on a separate branch. It has not been committed or published.

risks.title: Anyone can make themselves an admin
risks.explanation: The new role-change address never checks who is asking. The existing users list does check that the caller is an admin, but the new code skips that check. The sign-in check that guards the admin pages doesn't cover these addresses either. Anyone who knows a user's ID, or their own, can grant themselves admin rights without signing in. Add the same admin check the users list already uses before shipping.

risks.title: Anyone can permanently delete users and their shifts
risks.explanation: The new delete address also has no permission check. The database is set up so that deleting a user also deletes all of their shifts. An outsider or an ordinary staff member could wipe accounts and schedule history, and nothing in the app can undo it. Restrict this to admins, and make sure backups exist.

risks.title: Any text is accepted as a role
risks.explanation: The server saves whatever role value it receives, not just member, manager or admin. A bad or made-up value could lock someone out or confuse other permission checks. The server should only accept the three known roles.

risks.title: Admin gets no message if a change fails
risks.explanation: The page reloads the list after a change, whether it worked or not. If the change fails, the admin sees no error. They may think a role changed or a user was deleted when it wasn't. An admin could also delete or demote their own account by accident.

questions_for_developer: Can you add the same 'admin only' check to the new role-change and delete actions that the users list already has, and show me that a signed-out person gets refused?
Can the server reject any role other than member, manager or admin?
Should we stop admins from deleting or demoting themselves, or the last remaining admin?
Do we have database backups, so a mistaken user delete (which also removes their shifts) can be recovered?
good_news: The change is small and limited to the admin users screen, so the fix is quick: two permission checks and a role check.
The coding assistant spotted the missing permission check itself and held off committing it.
